screen === 'loading' — set synchronously inside runSearch() the instant a non-empty trimmed query fires (350ms after the last keystroke, via the debounce timer), before searchAll()'s promise settles

screen === 'error' — set only in searchAll(trimmed).catch(() => setScreen('error')), i.e. only if the promise returned by searchAll() rejects
uiStatesHandled.reachable: no — searchAll() in src/lib/api/search.ts wraps its apiFetch call in its own try/catch and always falls back to mockSearch(query) on any failure (network error, timeout, or MockModeError in mock mode), so the promise it returns to the page never rejects under any currently reachable code path. This .catch() is dead code today; it only becomes live once a real backend replaces the SEAM without also removing the internal fallback, or the fallback is changed to rethrow.

notes: No stubs.json entries reference this screen's files (src/app/(app)/search/page.tsx, src/lib/api/search.ts, src/lib/api/mocks/mockSearch.ts).

Follow (on creator rows) and Join (on community rows) buttons are rendered with no onClick handler at all in page.tsx — they are decorative in the current build, not wired to any action, mutation, or even a console log. No follow/join action exists for this screen.

The 'Clear' button on Recent searches only mutates local React state (setRecent([])) — there is no DELETE/clear call to /api/hub/search/recent, and no corresponding write endpoint is SEAM-tagged anywhere in search.ts. Likewise, recent-search history itself is entirely client-derived (pushed into local state after each successful search) with a GET SEAM for reading it but no POST/PUT seam for persisting a new entry server-side.

src/lib/api/search.ts also exports getSuggestedCommunities() (GET /api/hub/search/suggested-communities, backed by mockSearchCommunities), but this screen's page.tsx never calls it — it's dead/unused from this screen's perspective (out of scope for reads above).
